additional_original_rules_generalised.js.note: 5 confirmed-clean status pairs x 3 grammar types x 4 real topics (pulled from veerlosar's actual file) = 60 per category. Content-word substitutions where original failed tokenization: guarantee->promise, disclaimer->notice/note, Understood->Confirmed.

cultural_categories_verified_en.json.note: 5 cultural categories x 2 clause wordings x 4 topics x 5 status pairs x 3 grammar types = 120 each. Topics: medical, mental_health, legal, general -- no finance. All checkers are LLM-judge (no regex exists for tone/humor/directness/humility/emotion judgments).

cultural_imperative_declarative_en.json.note: All 30 queries per category individually authored, checked for duplicates within category before counting.

original_imperative_declarative_en.json.note: Imperative ('write 5 words') vs declarative ('5 words are written') mood contrast, no status tag -- the axis veerlosar/nuna originally proposed, not covered by the earlier 120-row sets (which varied status-word and register, never mood). Provenance per category noted below.

metadata.note: Hindi translation. check_native is False for ALL 2250 pairs: Hindi is outside the range Claude can self-verify (grammatical gender agreement, आप/तुम/तू register and verb conjugation, postpositions), so the entire file requires native review before use. GENDER HANDLING: (1) Assistant-voice text (all 750 persona correct_answers and the 60 ack_invert "Understood" tokens) was rewritten to be grammatically gender-neutral for the speaker — persona answers use an infinitive + "मेरा काम है" construction, and the Understood token is "ठीक है"; the "Confirmed" token "पुष्टि हुई" was already speaker-neutral. This removes a systematic masculine confound from the text the model must produce. (2) User-voice first-person utterances (35 distinct sentences that force a speaker gender) were balanced ~50/50 masculine/feminine via exact morphological mirrors (रहा हूँ/रही हूँ etc.) rather than left uniformly masculine. Native reviewers should still verify naturalness. Rules address the model informally (तुम); answers address the user politely. Hindi has no articles, so the single_word "no articles" rule is near-trivial.
